 Updated: 9:22 PM EST Nov 1, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Allen Cone Assignment Editor Angela Rozier Reporter STUART, Fla. — Early voting ended on the Treasure Coast and in Okeechobee County on Saturday for Tuesday's General Election. 
 Find your early voting location for Florida's 2026 general election In Palm Beach County, residents were still able to visit any of the 28 early polling sites on Sunday. 
 Advertisement On the Treasure Coast, the early voting totals are nearly 56,000 in St. Lucie County, around 29,000 each in Martin and Indian River counties, and more than 3,700 in Okeechobee County. 
 WPBF 25 Interactive Voter Guide for 2026 Florida general election In addition, residents statewide have the option to vote by mail.
 It was a busy day at the Martin County Supervisor of Elections Office in Stuart as workers wrapped up early voting. 
 "We've had a great turnout in Martin County," Vicki Davis told WPBF. 
 Martin County officials say more than 40% of registered voters cast their ballots by mail or during early voting. That's already higher than the overall 29% turnout in the primary. 
 After early voting, the only time to vote in person is on Election Day at their designated precinct. 
 Vote-by-mail ballots can be returned to county elections offices during business hours Monday or by 7 p.m. Sunday. Election officials don't go by postmarks. 
 "The biggest concern heading into Tuesday is voters knowing where their voting location is. So voters can access their voting location by going to our website at MartinVotes.gov or giving us a cal at 772-288-5637."
 'On the Record': Florida 2026 gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds More than 2.8 million of 13.7 million registered Floridians have already voted early, compared with over 50 million ballots cast nationwide ahead of Election Day. Also, around 1.8 million vote-by-mail ballots have been counted in Florida.
 In Palm Beach County, nearly 178,000 people have submitted their ballots early.
